title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
experiment: Turning off Adam's bias correction with β2 close to 1 makes the early steps several times larger than α, while with correction each step stays at about α. This is the initialization-bias mechanism of §3 and §5, and the trust-region bound of §2.1.
archetype_reason: Adam is one update rule repeated step by step, and the claim is about the size of each iteration's parameter step

fixed.objective: deterministic 1-D quadratic f(θ) = 0.5·θ², gradient g_t = θ_{t-1}
fixed.update_without_correction: same as above but m̂ = m_t and v̂ = v_t (RMSProp with momentum, as in section 6.4)

source.quote: In algorithm 1 we therefore divide by this term to correct the initialization bias.
the hyper-parameters β1, β2 ∈ [0, 1) control the exponential decay rates of these moving averages
Good default settings for the tested machine learning problems are α = 0.001, β1 = 0.9, β2 = 0.999
Since α sets (an upper bound of) the magnitude of steps in parameter space

metrics.name: max_step_ratio
metrics.label: largest step / α
metrics.meaning: maximum over t = 1..steps of |θ_t − θ_{t-1}| divided by α

reproduce.claim: With bias correction, every step has magnitude at most about α, even with β2 = 0.999.

source.quote: The effective magnitude of the steps taken in parameter space at each timestep are approximately bounded by the stepsize setting α

contrast.claim: Without bias correction and with β2 close to 1, the early steps are several times larger than α.

source.quote: not correcting the bias leads to very large stepsizes and often divergence
